news.title: Land transactions in India grow 66% CAGR since 2021: Report
news.para: India recorded 18,158 acres of land transactions across more than 880 deals in 33 cities between 2021 and Q1 2026, according to Cushman & Wakefield. The transacted land has potential to generate nearly 1.4 billion sq ft of built-up area and revenue worth about ₹16.67 lakh crore.

news.title: CAG audit finds ₹96 crore revenue leakage in Tamil Nadu's registration department
news.para: A recent CAG audit has unveiled concerning revenue leakages within Tamil Nadu's registration department, pointing to issues like property transaction undervaluation and misclassification. These discrepancies have led to a staggering potential loss exceeding ₹95 crore in 967 reported cases. Additionally, the audit highlights a lack of proper document correlation by registering officers, alongside a backlog in internal audits and unresolved audit paragraphs.

news.para: Residential Units Sealed For Commercial Use; Illegal Structures Demolished

news.title: Kolkata: KMC decided to shut down 919 lodges, guest houses, assures of fast-track reopening after fire compliance
news.para: The Kolkata Municipal Corporation is set to reopen over 900 previously closed lodges and guest houses. To ensure public safety, owners are required to upgrade their fire safety measures and comply with building codes. This decision follows a tragic fire incident at a crowded lodge on Free School Street.

news.title: Ranchi civic body's survey finds 1,300 hostels, lodges operating without licence
news.para: A recent survey highlighted that close to 1,300 hostels in Ranchi are operating without valid municipal licenses. This troubling discovery follows a tragic hostel collapse in Delhi, which claimed the lives of seven individuals. Many students are more focused on low costs and availability, neglecting the necessity for safety. Unlicensed hostels will face immediate scrutiny, with notices being issued regarding their building plans, requiring proper documents for future operations.

news.title: Rentomojo raises ₹376 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO
news.para: Rentomojo has successfully raised ₹376.07 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering. The firm issued over 9.3 million equity shares to 41 investors at a price of ₹404 each. The IPO is set to open for subscription from September 9 to September 11, 2026, with a price range established between ₹384 and ₹404 per share.

news.title: Pranav Constructions IPO subscribed 18.20 times on second day
news.para: On its second day, Pranav Constructions Ltd's initial public offering demonstrated exceptional enthusiasm from investors, with subscriptions soaring over eighteen times. Notably, non-institutional investors highlighted their considerable interest by subscribing forty-three times. Retail participation was vigorous as well, with their allocated shares reaching a subscription rate of fifteen times. Previously, the company successfully secured funding from anchor investors ahead of the share sale.

news.title: Enforcement directorate expands Suntec City probe, summons Mohali SSP
news.para: The Enforcement Directorate has summoned the Mohali SSP for details on a farmer cheating probe. This investigation concerns alleged fake consent letters used for Suntec City project permissions. The ED seeks information regarding police action and fresh offences flagged by the agency. Senior officials, including an IAS officer, have already been questioned by the ED. Former Punjab Chief Secretary Anurag Verma is also summoned for questioning soon.

news.title: Yes Bank fraud: CBI denied nod for further probe on Indiabulls Housing
news.para: A special court rejected the CBI's request for further investigation into Indiabulls and IVL Finance. The court found no material to warrant a fresh probe into the loan fraud case. CBI had previously stated there were no direct allegations of fund diversion by Indiabulls. The judge noted the agency's affidavit indicated no loss of public money. Consequently, the court deemed further investigation unnecessary for these entities.

news.title: Tata AIA Life leases nearly one lakh sq ft office in Thane’s Hiranandani Estate
news.para: Tata AIA Life Insurance has secured nearly 99,000 sq ft of office space in Thane under a lease agreement involving a rental commitment of around Rs 98 crore over nearly a decade. The agreement, which took effect in March 2026, includes an eight-month fit-out period, with rent payments scheduled to begin in November 2026. The deal highlights the growing demand for large office spaces in Thane’s expanding commercial market.

news.title: Mumbai ITAT allows tax relief on two flats bought as one home
news.para: Mumbai's Income-Tax Appellate Tribunal has declared that two flats can be categorized as a single residential house. This pivotal decision paves the way for taxpayers to leverage deductions under Section 54F of the Income-Tax Act. By emphasizing the functional use of the properties, the tribunal ensures that those who invest in multiple residences for their families can take full advantage of this beneficial tax provision.

news.title: Uttar Pradesh government constitutes panel to design rental housing model for seniors
news.para: In an effort to improve housing conditions for the elderly, the Uttar Pradesh government is setting up a specialized committee to create a rental housing policy. This committee will evaluate the specific needs of senior citizens and recommend an array of secured housing options. The policy aims to enhance affordability, safety, and accessibility, ultimately benefiting elderly residents who live on their own and promoting a more supportive living environment.

news.title: Maharashtra REAT orders demolition of additional wing in Ambernath housing project
news.para: Maharashtra Real Estate Appellate Tribunal ordered demolition of an additional project wing.  Promoters must pay a ten lakh rupee penalty for RERA and MOFA violations.  The tribunal directed restoration of open spaces as per the original plan.  Conveyance deed execution for the project land is also mandated within ninety days.  Promoters must also pursue increased water connections as per norms.

news.title: Karnataka high court orders Kaveri-2.0 fix after glitch blocks sale deeds
news.para: A recent court ruling has mandated that municipal authorities rectify the mapping of property records on the Kaveri 2.0 system. This ruling highlights failures in recognizing leasehold interests within digital documentation. The court underscored that technical glitches cannot obstruct legally transferrable leasehold rights. Authorities are now required to differentiate between primary owners and leaseholders within a two-month timeframe.

news.title: DHR Holdings leases 1.8 lakh sq ft office space in Bengaluru
news.para: DHR Holding India has leased nearly 1.8 lakh square feet of office space in Bengaluru. The company secured three floors at Sumadhura Capitol Towers for a five-year term. This fresh lease commenced on April 1, with a monthly rent of Rs 1.34 crore. The total rental outgo over five years is estimated at approximately Rs 88 crore. Bengaluru continues to see significant office leasing activity from multinational corporations.

news.title: SPVs set up under smart cities mission in Tamil Nadu reduced to funding conduits: CAG report
news.para: Critics have raised concerns about Tamil Nadu's Smart Cities Mission, highlighting that special purpose vehicles (SPVs) have become mere financial channels rather than independent entities. Public funding was misallocated to regular municipal projects outside of the planned development areas. Additionally, many expensive commercial projects sit unused, not bringing in the profits they promised.

news.title: Delhi civic body carries out demolition action against 24 properties
news.para: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi took significant steps by demolishing twenty-four properties and sealing seven illegal structures in an effort to enhance safety regulations. This initiative came in the wake of a disastrous building collapse in Satya Niketan, claiming seven lives. Reinforcement of laws was seen as officials inspected various paying guest accommodations for compliance, ordering structural audits to prevent future tragedies.

news.title: Delhi HC allows builders' body BAI to be party in CCI cement cartelisation case, dismisses UltraTech appeal
news.para: The Delhi High Court dismissed UltraTech Cement's appeal regarding the Builders Association of India's involvement.  The court affirmed the association's impleadment to aid the antitrust regulator's assessment.  This impleadment helps the Competition Commission of India reach a correct conclusion on allegations.  The Builders Association of India had also alleged cartelization by grey cement manufacturers.  The Competition Commission of India initiated an investigation after receiving market participant complaints.

news.title: Calcutta high court upholds conviction of developer for unauthorised construction
news.para: The Calcutta High Court has upheld the jail sentence of a developer found guilty of illegal construction, affirming that unlawful buildings in Kolkata endanger public safety. The court dismissed an appeal from both the developer and landowner, maintaining the initial three-year imprisonment assessed by the trial court while also adjusting the sentences accordingly.
